contracts.scope: Intel PIE startup graphs and bounded runtime dylib groups
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 little-endian LP64; guest calls/callbacks SysV64; host Windows APIs use their host ABI.
contracts.ownership: Mappings belong to loaded image groups. dlclose finalizes but retains mappings.
contracts.callbacks: Validate executable constructor/finalizer addresses; dependency-order construction and reverse teardown.
contracts.errors: Unsupported input fails before guest entry with worker exit125; guest exit codes preserved.
contracts.lifecycle: Resolve imports before mapping; relocate all images before constructors; join owned threads before unmapping.
contracts.unsupported: No shared cache, weak coalescing, dynamic TLV or dynamic Objective-C registration.

contracts.scope: C/POSIX locale, stream/format and jq/ripgrep-oriented POSIX adapters
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 little-endian LP64; guest calls/callbacks SysV64; host Windows APIs use their host ABI.
contracts.ownership: Guest FILE and host CRT stream are separate objects; never pass guest stat/tm/va_list to CRT.
contracts.callbacks: printf entry assembly captures SysV registers; no guest callback escapes the declared ABI.
contracts.errors: Per-thread Darwin errno; explicit ENOTSUP paths; errno mapping remains partial.
contracts.lifecycle: Session owns stream/environment state and flushes at exit; fopen/fclose manage individual streams.
contracts.unsupported: No Unicode locales, cookie streams, positional/wide/80-bit formatting or complete POSIX metadata/timezones.

contracts.scope: TLV, pthread lifecycle, keys, once, synchronization subset and the public static-initializer layouts
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 little-endian LP64; guest calls/callbacks SysV64; host Windows APIs use their host ABI.
contracts.ownership: Runtime owns thread tokens and per-thread storage; mutex/condition host objects are process-local.
contracts.callbacks: Start routines, key destructors and TLV destructors are SysV64; teardown permits bounded destructor re-registration.
contracts.errors: pthread APIs return Darwin error numbers; condition timedwait uses absolute guest deadlines.
contracts.lifecycle: Join owned threads before mapping teardown; run thread-local destruction and main-session cleanup.
contracts.unsupported: No cancellation, process-shared waiting, shared-cache TLV, robustness or scheduling-policy attributes, and no complete Darwin ordering proof; the same-binary suite covers the synchronized families only.

contracts.scope: Simple messages and bootstrap routing in local/broker namespaces
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 little-endian LP64; guest calls/callbacks SysV64; host Windows APIs use their host ABI.
contracts.ownership: Names refer to worker-owned rights; broker routes global endpoints and retires disconnected peers.
contracts.callbacks: Synchronous message APIs; no arbitrary host pointer or kernel handle passed as a guest right.
contracts.errors: XNU-style send/receive errors, header inversion, timeout and LARGE retry for supported operations.
contracts.lifecycle: Allocate/insert/deallocate within the owning namespace; send-once consumed; death invalidates routes.
contracts.unsupported: No complex/OOL/port descriptors, port sets, kernel enforcement, notifications or task APIs.

contracts.scope: Non-ObjC Blocks and Adapter-defined typed XPC between workers
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 little-endian LP64; guest calls/callbacks SysV64; host Windows APIs use their host ABI.
contracts.ownership: Copied handler blocks and typed objects are retained/released by runtime; no guest pointer serialized.
contracts.callbacks: SysV invoke on dispatcher thread; copied handlers remain alive through queued dispatch.
contracts.errors: Missing services and disconnected peers yield invalid/interrupted connection events.
contracts.lifecycle: Listener check-in, accepted peers, sync reply, cancellation and peer retirement are bounded implemented paths.
contracts.unsupported: No Apple wire interoperability, GCD/xpc_main, richer handles, ObjC captures, entitlements or security boundary.

contracts.scope: Five immutable runtime-created UTF-8 string functions
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 little-endian LP64; guest calls/callbacks SysV64; host Windows APIs use their host ABI.
contracts.ownership: Opaque runtime-owned strings; CF retain/release only for admitted objects.
contracts.callbacks: No callback-based collection or allocator interface exposed.
contracts.errors: Unsupported encoding or insufficient conversion space returns the implemented failure result.
contracts.lifecycle: Session owns the string registry; explicit retain/release changes references.
contracts.unsupported: No constant CF strings, collections, toll-free bridge, Foundation or runloop.

contracts.scope: Raw-isa startup Objective-C, protocols/properties, runtime-owned ARC/MRC strong and zeroing weak ownership, compiler ivar cleanup and recognized x64 return-value handoffs
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 little-endian LP64; guest calls/callbacks SysV64; host Windows APIs use their host ABI.
contracts.ownership: Runtime-owned instances have locked reference counts and allocation generations. RR adapters honor guest retain/release/autorelease methods; root entry points manipulate the counts. Final release marks deallocating before guest dealloc; object_dispose runs own .cxx_destruct methods subclass first, clears weak references, then frees. Strong stores retain new before releasing old. Weak slots are registered and zeroed, and loads pin objects while custom weak callbacks run outside the registry lock.
contracts.callbacks: SysV message IMPs and .cxx_destruct/weak/RR callbacks execute without the registry lock. Explicit thread-local autorelease pools drain in reverse order, including reentrant autoreleases to the draining pool; explicit pools are also drained during guest thread cleanup.
contracts.errors: Validate metadata before selector patching or constructors; unknown selector terminates125.
contracts.lifecycle: Register complete startup graph, load before C constructors; guard remains live through guest finalizers.
contracts.unsupported: No tagged/nonpointer isa, foreign or externally allocated objects, Objective-C Blocks ownership adapters, atomic/copy properties, associations, exceptions/ARC exception cleanup, C++ constructors, dynamic registration or shared cache. Unsupported x64 return-site patterns use retain/autorelease fallback and may extend temporary lifetimes; arbitrary custom weak/RR policies need further reference probes.

contracts.scope: Mach VM allocation, release and protection for the guest's own task
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 LP64; mach_vm_address_t and mach_vm_size_t are 64-bit, kern_return_t is a 32-bit int, task ports are 32-bit names.
contracts.ownership: An allocation is a host reservation recorded by the runtime; only recorded ranges are releasable.
contracts.errors: KERN_SUCCESS 0, KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS 1, KERN_PROTECTION_FAILURE 2, KERN_NO_SPACE 3, KERN_INVALID_ARGUMENT 4; task ports other than mach_task_self are refused.
contracts.lifecycle: Regions live until released or the run ends; release returns the host reservation to the operating system.
contracts.unsupported: No region queries, sharing, sub-range release, inheritance, ledger accounting, copy/read/write or purgeable flags.

contracts.scope: Synchronous Darwin signal dispositions, masks, pending sets, sigwait, raise/kill/killpg on the guest's own pid and default termination
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 LP64; sigset_t is a 32-bit mask with bit (signal - 1); handlers take (int) or (int, siginfo*, ucontext*) and are called with the latter two null.
contracts.ownership: Handler addresses are guest code; the adapter stores them and never frees or relocates them.
contracts.callbacks: Handlers run synchronously on the calling guest thread's stack with the signal and sa_mask blocked.
contracts.errors: EINVAL for signal 0, out of range, SIGKILL/SIGSTOP dispositions and unknown sigprocmask how; ESRCH for foreign pids and process groups; EPERM for pid -1; SIG_ERR from signal; sigwait returns EINVAL directly.
contracts.lifecycle: Dispositions and the mask live for the run; an unhandled terminating signal exits with 128 + signal.
contracts.unsupported: No asynchronous delivery, per-thread masks, siginfo/ucontext, sa_flags, alternate stacks, fault mapping, pthread_kill, sigsuspend, sigpause, sigset or sigvec.

contracts.scope: libdispatch queues, groups, once, after, apply, block objects, timer and user-data sources, and the Block runtime copy/dispose helpers
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 LP64; dispatch objects are opaque pointer-width tokens, dispatch_time_t is 64-bit (wall-clock values are the negated nanoseconds since the epoch), blocks follow the libclosure layout and are called with the block pointer as the first argument.
contracts.ownership: Queues, groups and sources are registry records reclaimed when their reference count is zero and no work is queued or running; submitted blocks are copied with Block_copy and released after they run; handler blocks are owned by their source until it is freed.
contracts.callbacks: Blocks and functions run on host worker threads set up like guest pthreads, on the calling thread for sync submission, or on the thread running dispatch_main for the main queue; destructors and finalizers run on a separate guest thread, never under the registry lock.
contracts.errors: Client bugs trap with exit status 132 and a diagnostic: sync onto a queue the thread already owns, unbalanced group leave, over-release, over-resume, resume of an inactive queue, invalid objects, NULL or non-executable blocks and functions. dispatch_get_global_queue and dispatch_source_create return NULL for unsupported arguments. Waits return 60 on timeout, matching the semaphore adapter.
contracts.lifecycle: State begins with the guest run; at normal exit queued work is discarded and running items finish before images are unmapped.
contracts.unsupported: Sources of type read, write, vnode, proc, signal, Mach and memory pressure; dispatch_data, dispatch_io and workloops; QoS scheduling and DISPATCH_BLOCK_BARRIER; root or main queue as a target; ordering of apply on serial queues.

contracts.scope: pthread and libsystem quality-of-service classes recorded per thread and attribute
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 LP64; qos_class_t is a 32-bit unsigned value (0x21, 0x19, 0x15, 0x11, 0x09); relative priorities are in -15..0.
contracts.ownership: The class is stored in the guest's pthread_attr_t reserved bytes at offsets 16 and 20; the adapter owns no other state.
contracts.errors: EINVAL for unknown classes, relative priorities outside -15..0 and uninitialised attributes; override start returns NULL on invalid input.
contracts.lifecycle: Per-thread records start at user-interactive for the main thread and default for other threads and end with the thread.
contracts.unsupported: No scheduling effect, no application of an attribute's class by pthread_create, no reading of another thread's class, no real overrides.

contracts.scope: sysctl, sysctlbyname and sysctlnametomib over host-derived and fixed Darwin values, plus libproc queries about the guest's own process
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 LP64; MIB components are 32-bit ints, lengths are size_t, integer values are 32-bit unless the header documents a 64-bit byte count or frequency, strings include their NUL.
contracts.ownership: Returned values are copied into the caller's buffer; the adapter keeps only a lazily built name table and cached processor information.
contracts.errors: -1 with errno: ENOENT for unknown names and MIBs, EPERM for any write, ENOMEM for a short buffer or MIB array (the required size is still reported), EINVAL for NULL names, MIB lengths outside 2..12 and undersized libproc buffers, ESRCH for libproc pids other than the guest's. libproc functions return 0 on error.
contracts.lifecycle: Values are computed at call time except processor information, which is read once.
contracts.unsupported: kern.proc and kern.procargs2, kern.clockrate, vm.vmmeter, net.* and debug.* subtrees, disk statistics, performance levels, writes, libproc process listing by other filters, file-descriptor and region flavors, proc_pid_rusage and dirty tracking.

contracts.scope: Loaded-image containment and compact/DWARF section discovery for startup and runtime dlopen images; no stack walking or exceptions
contracts.calling_convention: Darwin x86-64 SysV; bool in AL; dyld_unwind_sections is five LP64 pointer/length words (40 bytes, align8).
contracts.ownership: Borrowed pointers into mapped images and stable registry CString paths; no allocations returned to caller. Sections remain valid while the mapping exists. Runtime dlclose retains mappings in the existing loader subset.
contracts.callbacks: No callbacks. Dynamic image records are published before plugin constructors.
contracts.errors: Unknown/unmapped address returns false or null. A failed unwind query leaves the output buffer unchanged; a recognized image succeeds even with no unwind sections. Unwind sections must be unique, file-backed readable __TEXT ranges with consistent VM/file offsets; malformed metadata rejects execution before constructors.
contracts.lifecycle: Build relocated section/range records from validated image plans at startup and append for dlopen groups before initialization. No independent host-module or shared-cache registration.
contracts.unsupported: No FDE/index decoding, compact encoding interpretation, DWARF CFI execution, personalities, exception propagation, host-frame unwinding, JIT/shared-cache images or true unload. Invalid output-pointer behavior is not claimed as a Darwin equivalence.
